stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

from collections import Counter
import json

def f(gin):
    H,W=len(gin),len(gin[0])
    cnt=Counter(x for r in gin for x in r)
    bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    others=[x for x in set(cnt) if x!=bg]
    # noise = most frequent non-bg color
    noise=max(others,key=lambda x:cnt[x])
    # find pair runs (consecutive same-value runs of len>=2, value in {2,3})
    pairs=[]
    for i,r in enumerate(gin):
        j=0
        while j<W:
            if r[j]!=bg and r[j]!=noise:
                k=j
                while k<W and r[k]==r[j]: k+=1
                if r[j] in (2,3) and k-j==2:
                    pairs.append((r[j],i,j))
                j=k
            else:
                j+=1
    pairs.sort()
    (vA,rA,cA),(vB,rB,cB)=pairs
    top,bottom=min(rA,rB),max(rA,rB)
    channels=[c for c in range(W) if all(gin[r][c]==bg for r in range(top+1,bottom))]
    out=[row[:] for row in gin]
    best=None
    for c in channels:
        ok=True
        # segment on each pair row, between pair and channel, must be bg
        def seg_ok(ccA):
            lo,hi=min(ccA,c)+0,0
            a,b=(ccA,c) if ccA<c else (c,ccA)
            return all(gin[r][x]==bg for x in range(a+1,b))
        if seg_ok(rA) and seg_ok(rB):
            best=c
    K=best
    assert K is not None
    for r in range(top+1,bottom):
        out[r][K]=3
    def fill(cc):
        a,b=(cc,K) if cc<K else (K,cc)
        for x in range(a+1,b): out[a_r_or_b][x]=3
    for val,(r,cc) in [(vA,rA,cA),(vB,rB,cB)]:
        fill(cc)
    return out

def f(gin):
    H,W=len(gin),len(gin[0])
    cnt=Counter(x for r in gin for x in r); bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    noise=[x for x in set(cnt) if x!=bg]
    pairs=[]
    for i,r in enumerate(gin):
        j=0
        while j<W-1:
            if r[j]==r[j+1] and r[j] not in (bg,noise):
                val=r[j]; j2=j
                while j2<W and r[j2]==val: j2+=1
                pairs.append((val,i,j,j2-1))
                j=j2
            else: j+=1
    pairs.sort(key=lambda p:p[1]); A,B=pairs[0],pairs[1]
    top,bottom=min(A[1],B[1]),max(A[1],B[1])
    out=[row[:] for row in gin]
    # channels strictly between the two rows
    ch=[c for c in range(W) if all(gin[r][c]==bg for r in range(top+1,bottom))]
    best=None
    for c in ch:
        ok=True
        if A[1]<B[1]:
            ta,tb=A; tb_=B
            lo,hi=(ta[3]+1,c)
            if not all(gin[A[1]][x]==bg for x in range(lo,hi+1)): ok=False
            lo,hi=(tb[3]+1,c)
            if not all(gin[B[1]][x]==bg for x in range(lo,hi+1)): ok=False
        else:
            tb_,ta=B,A
            lo,hi=(ta[3]+1,c)
            if not all(gin[A[1]][x]==bg for x in range(lo,hi+1)): ok=False
            lo,hi=(tb[3]+1,c)
            if not all(gin[B[1]][x]==bg for x in range(lo,hi+1)): ok=False
        if ok: best=c; break
    if best is None: return out
    for r in range(top+1,bottom): out[r][best]=3
    toprow=[A if A[1]<B[1] else B]
    bot=[B if A[1]<B[1] else A]
    for v,(r,k,s) in [(toprow[0],[A[1],A[2],A[3]]),(bot[0],[B[1],B[2],B[3]])]:
        lo,hi=(k+1,best) if k<best else (best,k+1)
        for x in range(lo,hi+1): out[r][x]=3
    return out

    cnt=Counter(x for r in gin for x in r); bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    noise=[x for x in set(cnt) if x!=bg]
    pairs=[]
    for i,r in enumerate(gin):

            if r[j]==r[j+1] and r[j] not in (bg,noise):
                val=r[j]; j2=j
                while j2<W and r[j2]==val: j2+=1

import os,glob,re,json
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    base=d+'/../../sessions'
    G={}
    for fp in glob.glob(base+'/*.jsonl'):
        t=open(fp,errors='ignore').read().replace('\\n','\n')
        for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
            k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
            rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
            if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
                G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load(); print(sorted(G))
ti=G.get('Test input'); print(ti is not None)
for n in range(1,9):
    i=G[f'Demo pair {n} input']; o=G[f'Demo pair {n} output']
    print(f'--- pair {n}: in {len(i)}x{len(i[0])} out {len(o)}x{len(o[0])}')
    # check equal lengths per side comparison
    H=len(i); W=len(i[0])
    if len(o)>W:
        # find best offset alignment between out and in
        import collections
        best=[]
        for dr in range(-len(o)+1,H+1):
            for dc in range(W-len(o)+1):
                # count matching non-bg cells relative
                bg=collections.Counter(v for r in i for v in r).most_common(1)[0][0]
                sc=sum(1 for r in range(H) for c in range(min(W,len(o))) if dr>=0 and r+dr<H and i[r][c]==o[r+dr][c+dc])
                best.append((sc,dr,dc))
        best.sort(reverse=True)
        print(' best overlap offsets',best[:3])

from collections import deque, Counter

def solve(gi):
    R,C=len(gi),len(gi[0])
    cnt=Counter(x for r in gi for x in r); bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    # objects: bars of the two special colors (not bg, not the dominant noise color)
    vals=sorted(set(x for r in gi for x in r)-{bg})
    noise=max((x,c) for x,c in cnt.items() if x!=bg)[0]
    specials=[x for x in vals if x!=noise]
    A=[(r,c) for r in range(R) for c in range(C) if gi[r][c]==specials[0]]
    B=[(r,c) for r in range(R) for c in range(C) if gi[r][c]==specials[1]]
    out=[row[:] for row in gi]
    # extend A along its axis toward B until blocked; fill with 3
    ar=A[0]; br=B[0]
    # determine orientation of A: vertical if columns equal else horizontal
    verticalA = len({a[1] for a in A})==1
    # direction along axis toward B: compare midpoint
    mA=(sum(a[0] for a in A)/2, sum(a[1] for a in A)/2)
    mB=(sum(b[0] for b in B)/2, sum(b[1] for b in B)/2)
    def extend(start, vertical, towardsB):
        # start = first cell of bar; move along axis in sign(deltar or ddc) toward B
        cells=[]; r,c=start
        dr,dv = (1,0) if vertical else (0,1)
        if towardsB:
            sgn_r = 1 if mB[0]>mA[0] else -1
            sgn_c = 1 if mB[1]>mA[1] else -1
            dirvec = (sgn_r, sgn_c) if vertical else None
            # for vertical bar, axis is rows
            dr,dc = sgn_r, 0
        n,r,c=start
        while True:
            nr,nc=n+dr,c+dc
            if not (0<=nr<R and 0<=nc<C) or gi[nr][nc]!=bg: break
            cells.append((nr,nc)); n+=1
        return cells
    extA=extend(A[0],verticalA,True)
    for r,c in extA: out[r][c]=3
    extB=extend(B[0], len({b[1] for b in B})==1, True)
    for r,c in extB: out[r][c]=3
    # connector: from bottom end of A's extension go horizontally toward B's column, then down to B's top
    # find connection points
    endA = extA[-1]
    colB = {b[1] for b in B}
    # move right/left from endA to colB along same row, if that row is bg at all
    rr=endA[0]
    cc=min(colB,key=lambda x:abs(x-endA[1]))
    rowcells=[]; n,c=endA
    while c!=cc:

        if not(0<=nc<C) or gi[n][nc]!=bg: return None
        rowcells.append((n,nc)); c=nc
    for p in rowcells: out[p[0]][p[1]]=3
    # vertical connector from (rr,cc) to B's ray: fill gap
    botB=min(b[0] for b in B)
    for r in range(rr,botB): out[r][cc]=3
    return out

from collections import deque
def bfs_path(I,start,end):
    H,W=len(I),len(I[0])
    cnt=Counter(x for r in I for x in r); bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    q=deque([start]); seen={start}
    while q:
        i,j=q.popleft()
        if (i,j)==end: return seen
        for di,dj in [(-1,0),(1,0),(0,-1),(0,1)]:
            ni,nj=i+di,j+dj
            if 0<=ni<H and 0<=nj<W and I[ni][nj]==bg and (ni,nj) not in seen:
                seen.add((ni,nj)); q.append((ni,nj))
    return None
for p in ['3','4','5']:
    I_=G[f'Demo pair {p} input']; O_=G[f'Demo pair {p} output']
    H,W=len(I_),len(I_[0])
    chg=set((i,j) for i in range(H) for j in range(W) if I_[i][j]!=O_[i][j])
    cnt=Counter(x for r in I_ for x in r); bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    m=[c for c,n in cnt.items() if n==2]
    ms=[[(i,j) for i,r in enumerate(I_) for j,x in enumerate(r) if x==c][0] for c in m]
    s,e=ms[0],ms[1]   # reading order
    S=set(bfs_path(I_,s,e))
    print(p,'s=',s,'e=',e,'|S|= ',len(S),'|chg|=',len(chg),'exact?',S==chg)
    if S!=chg and S:
        print('  extra:',sorted(S-chg)[:8],'missed:',sorted(chg-S)[:8])

from collections import deque, Counter
from itertools import product

def monotone_paths(I,start,end):
    H,W=len(I),len(I[0])
    cnt=Counter(x for r in I for x in r); bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    dr=1 if end[0]>start[0] else -1; dc=1 if end[1]>start[1] else -1
    dR=(end[0]-start[0])//abs(dr); dC=(end[1]-start[1])//abs(dc)
    # monotone only allowed directions
    dirs=[(dr,0),(0,dc)] if (dr!=0 and dc!=0) else [(dr,0)] if dr!=0 else [(0,dc)]
    # generate all sequences of dR steps of dir0 and dC steps of dir1 (mixed orderings)
    steps=[]
    for _ in range(dR): steps.append(dirs[0]); 
    return None
# simpler: brute force all shortest monotone routes via recursion with pruning; but number of combos = binom(dR+dC, dR) may be large. Instead use DP: reachable set of cells at each step; record predecessors.
def route_dp(I,start,end):
    H,W=len(I),len(I[0])
    cnt=Counter(x for r in I for x in r); bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    dr=1 if end[0]>=start[0] else -1; dc=1 if end[1]>=start[1] else -1
    dR=abs(end[0]-start[0]); dC=abs(end[1]-start[1])
    dirs=[(dr,0),(0,dc)]
    cur={start}; par={}
    for s in range(dR+dC):
        nxt=set()
        for (i,j) in cur:
            for (di,dj) in dirs:
                ni,nj=i+di*s if False else i+dirs[s%2][0]  # placeholder
        break
    return None

from collections import deque, Counter

def solve_g(I):
    H,W=len(I),len(I[0])
    cnt=Counter(x for r in I for x in r); bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    mcolors=[c for c,n in cnt.items() if n==2]
    noise={c for c in cnt if c not in {bg,*mcolors}}
    mcells=[(i,j) for i,r in enumerate(I) for j,x in enumerate(r) if x in mcolors]
    src,tgt=min(mcells),max(mcells)
    # BFS shortest path through cells not in noise (markers are passable)
    q=deque([src]); seen={src}; parent={}
    while q:
        (i,j)=q.popleft()
        if (i,j)==tgt: break
        for di,dj in [(-1,0),(1,0),(0,-1),(0,1)]:
            ni,nj=i+di,j+dj
            if 0<=ni<H and 0<=nj<W and (ni,nj) not in seen and I[ni][nj] not in noise:
                seen.add((ni,nj)); parent[(ni,nj)]=(i,j); q.append((ni,nj))
    path=[]; cur=tgt
    while cur!=src:
        cur=parent[cur]; path.append(cur)
    path=list(reversed(path))
    O=[r[:] for r in I]
    for i,j in path: O[i][j]=3
    return O,path

# verify all demos
for p in ['3','4','5','6']:
    I_=G[f'Demo pair {p} input']; O_=G[f'Demo pair {p} output']
    pth=solve_g(I_)
    print(p,'match:',pth[0]==O_,'path len',len(pth[1]))
# Test input
Ti=G['Test input']; print('Test path:')
print(solve_g(Ti)[1])

from collections import deque, Counter

def solve_g(I):
    H,W=len(I),len(I[0])
    cnt=Counter(x for r in I for x in r); bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    mcolors=[c for c,n in cnt.items() if n==2]
    noise={c for c in cnt if c not in {bg,*mcolors}}
    mcells=[(i,j) for i,r in enumerate(I) for j,x in enumerate(r) if x in mcolors]
    src,tgt=min(mcells),max(mcells)
    si_,sj_=src; ti_,tj_=tgt
    O=[r[:] for r in I]
    # greedy monotone walk: prefer moving toward target along primary axis; when blocked, turn
    # directions prioritized: towards target
    dirs=[(0,1),(1,0),(-1,0),(0,-1)]
    dr=(ti_>=si_)-(ti_<=si_); dc=(tj_>=sj_)
    # prefer axis aligned with larger gap? use target-relative priority: prefer horizontal if col gap bigger else vertical? try: prefer direction with positive component toward target, among them the one with largest projection
    dvec=lambda di,dj:(dr*di,dc*dj)
    order=sorted([d for d in [(-1,0),(1,0),(0,-1),(0,1)]], key=lambda d:(-(abs(d[0]*dr)+abs(d[1]*dc)), -(abs(dr*d[0])+abs(dc*d[1]))) if (d[0]*dr or d[1]*dc) else -10)
    order=[d for d in [(0,1),(0,-1),(1,0),(-1,0)] if (d[0]==dr or d[1]==dc) and (d[0]*dr>0 or d[1]*dc>0)][:1]+ \
          [d for d in [(0,1),(0,-1),(1,0),(-1,0)] if (d[0]==dr or d[1]==dc) and (d[0]*dr>0 or d[1]*dc>0)][1:]
    order=[d for d in [(0,1),(1,0),(-1,0),(0,-1)] if (d[0]*dr>0 or d[1]*dc>0)][:2]+[d for d in [(0,1),(1,0),(-1,0),(0,-1)] if (d[0]*dr>0 or d[1]*dc>0)][2:]
    cur=src
    while True:
        moved=False
        for di,dj in order:
            ni,nj=cur[0]+di,cur[1]+dj
            if 0<=ni<H and 0<=nj<W and I[ni][nj]!=noise[0] if False else I[ni][nj]!=list(noise)[0]:
                pass
        break
    return None

def solve(I):
    H,W=len(I),len(I[0])
    cnt=Counter(x for r in I for x in r); bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    bar2=set((a,b) for a in range(H) for b in range(W) if I[a][b]==2)
    bar3=set((a,b) for a in range(H) for b in range(W) if I[a][b]==3)
    O=[r[:] for r in I]
    # BFS distances (4-conn, bg only)
    dist={}
    q=deque()
    for s in bar2: dist[s]=0; q.append(s)
    while q:
        (x,y)=q.popleft(); d=dist[(x,y)]
        if (x,y) in bar3: break
        for dx,dy in((0,1),(0,-1),(1,0),(-1,0)):
            n=(x+dx,y+dy)
            if not(0<=n[0]<H and 0<=n[1]<W) or I[n[0]][n[1]]!=bg or n in bar2: continue
            if n not in dist: dist[n]=d+1; q.append(n)
    tgt=min(bar3,key=lambda p:dist.get(p,float('inf')))
    if tgt not in dist: return None
    # collect all shortest paths via parent tracking; take lexicographically smallest path
    P=set()
    for start in bar2:
        # parents in a shortest path from start to tgt
        par={}
        qq=deque([start]); par[start]=None
        while qq:
            (x,y)=qq.popleft()
            if (x,y)==tgt: break
            for dx,dy in((0,1),(0,-1),(1,0),(-1,0)):
                n=(x+dx,y+dy)
                if not(0<=n[0]<H and 0<=n[1]<W) or I[n[0]][n[1]]!=bg or n in bar2: continue
                if n not in par and dist[n]==dist[(x,y)]+1:
                    par[n]=(x,y); qq.append(n)
        # backtrace from tgt
        cur=tgt
        while cur is not None and cur not in bar2:
            prev=par[cur]; cur=prev
        if cur is None: continue
        path=list(cur)
        while path and path[-1] not in bar2:
            prev=par[path[-1]]; path.append(prev)
        if path and path[0] in bar2 and path[-1]==tgt: P.add(tuple(path))
    best=min(P)
    for a,b in best:
        if I[a][b]==bg: O[a][b]=3
    return O,best

from collections import deque
def f(I):
    H,W=len(I),len(I[0])
    bg=Counter(x for r in I for x in r).most_common(1)[0][0]
    bar2=[(a,b) for a in range(H) for b in range(W) if I[a][b]==2]
    bar3=[(a,b) for a in range(H) for b in range(W) if I[a][b]==3]
    dist={}; P={}
    q=deque()
    for s in bar2: dist[s]=0; P[s]=None; q.append(s)
    while q:
        (x,y)=q.popleft()
        if any(abs(a-x)+abs(b-y)==1 for a,b in bar3): break
        for dx,dy in((0,1),(0,-1),(1,0),(-1,0)):
            n=(x+dx,y+dy)
            if not(0<=n[0]<H and 0<=n[1]<W) or n in dist: continue
            # allow crossing bar2 cells but not bar3 yet
            if n in bar3: continue
            d=dists:=dist[(x,y)]+1
            if d<dist.get(n,999): dist[n]=d; P[n]=(x,y); q.append(n)
    cands=[]
    for (a,b) in bar3:
        for dx,dy in((0,1),(0,-1),(1,0),(-1,0)):
            p=(a+dx,b+dy)
            if p in dist: cands.append((dist[p],p))
    cands.sort()
    _,end=cands[0]
    O=[r[:] for r in I]
    cur=end
    while cur not in bar2:
        if I[cur[0]][cur[1]]==bg: O[cur[0]][cur[1]]=3
        cur=P[cur]
    return O
